Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City 20 2023 http: //vvww.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 46 s. 2023 HON. EDGARDO F. ARCAY Mayor Panglao, Bohol Dear Mayor Arcay: This has reference to your letter dated February 13, 2023 requesting the Department's clarification on whether a Sanggunian Resolution can pre-terminate contracts of service which had been renewed by the local chief executive (LCE) without prior authority of the sanggunian. Per the representation, the antecedent facts are as follows: • On July 11, 2022, the Sangguniang Bayan of Panglao, Bohol adopted Resolution No. 107, s. 2022 entitled: A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE LOCAL CHIEF EXECUTIVE, HONORABLE EDGARDO F. ARCAY TO HIRE THE MEMBERS WHO WOULD COMPOSE THE PANGLAO ADVISORY TEAM (PAT) PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 01, SERIES OF 2022. • Pursuant to the authority granted, you entered into individual contracts of services with 12 members of the advisory team. They served the municipality from July 12 to December 31, 2022. • Resolution No. 107 did not expressly stipulate the duration of such authority granted by the sanggunian. • On January 1, 2023, you renewed the contracts of the PAT members for another six (6) months until June 30, 2023. • On January 23, 2023, Vice Mayor Noel L. Hormachuelos wrote your Office, together with the PAT members, to attend a meeting where one of the agenda was the proposed resolution recalling Resolution No. 107. On January 30, 2023, during session of the sanggunian, the body passed Resolution No. 24, s. 2023 entitled "A RESOLUTION SUPERSEDING RESOLUTION NO. 107, SERIES OF 2022, ENDING THE CONTRACTS THAT EMANATE FROM IT BY JANUARY 31ST 2023, AND NECESSITATING A NEW RESOLUTION FOR THEIR POSSIBLE RENEWAL. • Resolution No. 24 further provides that those who are deserving and whose positions are necessary under a new resolution shall start on February 1, 2023, if they report in office in such date, otherwise those contracts shall start on the day they first report in officer under their new contracts. • In your letter, you maintained that PAT members' contracts were renewed in good faith on the basis of Resolution 107 and that Resolution No. 24 unilaterally pre-terminated the existing contracts. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

• Hence, you are now in quandary as to which between Resolution No. 24 and the existing Contracts of Services must prevail. The authority of the Local Government Unit (LGU) to engage the services of individuals under contract of services is governed by Sections 77 and 444(b)(1)(vi) of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), viz: Section 77. Responsibility for Human Resources and Development. - The chief executive of every local government unit shall be responsible for human resources and development in his unit and shall take all personnel actions in accordance with the Constitutional provisions on civil service, pertinent laws, and rules and regulations thereon, including such policies, guidelines and standards as the Civil Service Commission may establish: Provided, That the local chief executive may employ emergency or casual employees or laborers paid on a daily wage or piecework basis and hired through job orders for local projects authorized by the sanggunian concerned, without need of approval or attestation by the Civil Service Commission: Provided, further, That the period of employment of emergency or casual laborers as provided in this Section shall not exceed six (6) months. Section 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (vi) Upon authorization by the Sangguniang Bayan, represent the municipality in all its business transactions and sign on its behalf all bonds, contracts, and such other documents made pursuant to law or ordinance. (Emphasis ours) Consequently, the exercise of the LGU's power to enter into contracts is subject to compliance with Section 22(c) of the LGC, which provides: Section 22. Corporate powers — xxx (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or city, municipal or barangay hall. Applying the foregoing, prior authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan of Panglao is indeed necessary in order for you to enter into contract of services anew with member of the PAT team. Corollarily, contracts entered into by the LCE without the requisite prior authority from the sanggunian shall make the contract unenforceable. Article 1317 of the Civil Code provides the definition of an unenforceable contract, thus: "ART. 1317. A contract entered into in the name of another by one who has no authority or legal Page 2 of 4

representation, or who has acted beyond his powers, shall be unenforceable, unless it is ratified, expressly or impliedly, by the person on whose behalf it has been executed, before it is revoked by the other contracting party." In University of Mindanao, Inc. vs. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, et al.l, the Supreme Court explained the rationale in rendering contracts unenforceable: "The unenforceable status of contracts entered into by an unauthorized person on behalf of another is based on the basic principle that contracts must be consented to by both parties. There is no contract without meeting of the minds as to the subject matter and cause of the obligations created under the contract. Consent of a person cannot be presumed from representations of another, especially if obligations will be incurred as a result. Thus, authority is required to make actions made on his or her behalf binding on a person. Contracts entered into by persons without authority from the corporation shall generally be considered ultra vires and unenforceable against the corporation." However, such defect is not without a remedy. Article 1403 of the Civil Code also provides that unenforceable contracts may be ratified expressly or impliedly, thus: "ART. 1403. The following contracts are unenforceable, unless they are ratified: (I) Those entered into in the name of another person by one who has been given no authority or legal representation, or who has acted beyond his powers[.]" Meanwhile, based on records, there appears to be an implied ratification on the part of the Sangguniang Bayan of Panglao, thus: (1) following the renewal of the contracts of the PAT members on January 1, 2023, the PAT members as well as the Honorable Mayor were invited by the August Body for a meeting on January 25, 2023, (2) Resolution 24 likewise, granted you the authority to renew the contracts of the PAT members, albeit ending the existing contracts of some by January 31, 2023, and (3) one of the WHEREAS Clauses of Resolution No. 24 states: "WHEREAS, the contracts of those already renewed under Resolution No. 107, s. 2022 shall end on January 31st 2023, and for those who are deserving and whose positions are necessary under a new resolution shall start on February ISt 2023, if they report in office in such date, otherwise, those contracts shall start on the day they first report in office under their new contracts." Thus, applying Article 1403 of the Civil Code, these actions of the sanggunian appears to operate as affirmation or acceptance of the contracts which had already been entered into by the Mayor as ratification. 1 G.R. No. 194964, January 11, 2016. Page 3 of 4

This opinion is based on facts as represented and it will be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have clarified you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY. J AN CTOR R.
